study.plan: NYC Heat Emergency Plan (NYCEM / DOHMH), as published 2024-2026
study.zones_source: NYC Department of City Planning, Community Districts (59, excluding Joint Interest Areas such as parks and airports, which have no resident population). AOI reduced to the 346 sq mi land-heavy box that the API accepts: a 840 sq mi box spanning the full five boroughs includes open ocean, New York Harbor and Long Island Sound and is REJECTED by /v1/heatmap with a FortyGuardError. Districts whose centroid falls outside the reduced box are excluded rather than silently returned with no tile coverage.
study.timezone_note: New York is UTC-4 during Eastern Daylight Time, which covers the entire summer heat season. Unlike Arizona, New York does observe DST, so this offset is correct for the study window but not year-round.

summary.baseline: citywide proxy (area-weighted AOI mean) - a stand-in for station-based sensing, not a station feed
summary.framing: One flaw, two failure modes, severity-dependent. A trigger keyed to a single fixed number under-fires where the citywide mean sits below it and over-fires where severity clears it everywhere at once. Saturation is the mechanism; lost coverage is the consequence.

population_source: US Census ACS 5-year 2023 block groups, areally interpolated onto village boundaries

clauses.action: Declare an extreme heat event and activate the Heat Emergency Plan: open cooling centres across the five boroughs, expand outreach to at-risk residents, and coordinate with healthcare providers and utilities.
clauses.source_text: New York City defines extreme heat events as periods when the heat index is 100°F or higher for one or more days, or 95°F or higher for two or more consecutive days.
actor: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene

clauses.action: Declare an extreme heat event when the 95°F condition holds on two or more consecutive days, and activate the Heat Emergency Plan.
clauses.source_text: New York City defines extreme heat events as periods when the heat index is 100°F or higher for one or more days, or 95°F or higher for two or more consecutive days.
actor: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene

clauses.action: Public guidance benchmark: the level at which the City tells residents heat becomes especially dangerous.
clauses.source_text: A heat index above 95°F is especially dangerous.

axes.x: severity_c - mean tile temperature over the AOI that day, degC
axes.y: targeting_bits - binary entropy of the firing share, 0 to 1. 1 bit when the trigger splits the city evenly, 0 bits when it says the same thing everywhere. This is the axis that collapses at BOTH ends of severity.
axes.y_alt: discrimination - distinct values as a share of tiles. Weak at city scale: 272,917 floats always carry tens of thousands of distinct values, so it never reaches zero however useless the trigger is.

severity_sweep.caveat: The published window was selected for severity, so it samples the hot end of the range only. A wide severity span is needed to observe both arms of the curve; the span actually covered is reported above.

percentile.note: p90 of that day's own tile distribution. Post hoc: a deployable version would use a percentile of historical climatology, not of the day being judged.
